The Rays evened the ALCS at 1-1 with a 3-1 win over the Guardians at Tropicana Field, powered by a decisive fourth-inning rally. The best-of-7 series shifts with no team facing elimination in Game 3.

  • Liam Hicks [2-3 | RC 76] delivered the decisive blow in the bottom of the 4th, lining a two-run single to center that scored Chandler Simpson [1-3 | RC 68] and Ben Williamson [0-1, 1 BB] to put Tampa Bay up 3-0 in an eventual 3-1 win over Cleveland. (TB)
  • Freddy Peralta [6 IP, 0 ER, 6 K | 4.42 ERA, PAR 31] was dominant for the Rays, tossing six shutout innings with six strikeouts. (TB)
  • Parker Messick [5 IP, 0 ER, 3 K | 2.56 ERA, PAR 66] matched zeros for five innings in the loss, striking out three. (CLE)
  • Jonny DeLuca [2-4 | RC 45] and Hicks each had multi-hit games for Tampa Bay. (TB)
  • Chase DeLauter [1-2, 2 BB | RC 82] and Steven Kwan [2-5 | RC 72] led the Guardians at the plate. (CLE)

The Milwaukee Brewers took a commanding 2-0 lead in the NLCS with a win over the Dodgers, while the Guardians stole Game 1 of the ALCS from the Rays in Tampa after trailing late. Cleveland's comeback produced the day's biggest WPA swing.

  • Christian Yelich [2-5 | RC 53]'s two-run single in the bottom of the 3rd put Milwaukee ahead for good, and the Brewers beat the Dodgers 7-4 to go up 2-0 in the NLCS. (MIL)
  • Chase DeLauter [3-4, 1 BB, 1 HR | RC 82]'s go-ahead double in the top of the 8th capped Cleveland's rally from a 2-1 deficit, lifting the Guardians over the Rays 7-3 for a 1-0 ALCS lead. (CLE)
  • Drew Rasmussen [6 IP, 2 ER, 7 K | 2.67 ERA, PAR 62] was dominant in the loss, posting the day's top pitching line for Tampa Bay. (TB)
  • William Contreras [3-4, 1 BB, 1 HR | RC 80] led the Brewers' offense with a 3-for-4 night and a home run. (MIL)
  • Patrick Bailey [2-4, 1 HR | RC 28] homered as part of Cleveland's attack, backing DeLauter's big game. (CLE)

The Milwaukee Brewers took Game 1 of the NLCS, rallying from an early deficit to beat the Dodgers 2-1 at American Family Field and grab a 1-0 series lead. The game turned on a late-innings defensive stand that preserved the one-run win.

  • Mookie Betts [1-4, 1 BB | RC 71] flied out to center fielder Garrett Mitchell [0-3, 1 BB | RC 68] in the top of the 9th, sealing Milwaukee's 2-1 Game 1 win over Los Angeles. (LAD)
  • Tarik Skubal [5 IP, 2 ER, 7 K | 2.73 ERA, PAR 59] was sharp over 5 innings for the Dodgers in a losing effort. (LAD)
  • Jacob Misiorowski [4.1 IP, 1 ER, 5 K | 1.81 ERA, PAR 78] matched him with a strong start for Milwaukee. (MIL)
  • Brice Turang [1-2, 1 BB, 1 HR | RC 96] supplied the key offense for the Brewers with a home run. (MIL)
  • The Brewers' bullpen trio of Aaron Ashby [2 IP, 0 ER, 1 K | 3.13 ERA, PAR 28], Abner Uribe [1 IP, 0 ER, 2 K | 1.98 ERA, PAR 24], and company shut the door late. (MIL)

The Cleveland Guardians clinched the AL Division Series with a 2-0 win over the Chicago White Sox, taking the best-of-five series 3-2 and eliminating Chicago. The decisive blow came from José Ramírez [1-3, 1 BB, 1 HR | RC 56], whose fourth-inning homer provided all the runs Cleveland needed.

  • José Ramírez broke the scoreless tie with a two-run homer to right field in the bottom of the 4th, scoring Steven Kwan [1-3, 1 BB | RC 72] and giving Cleveland a 2-0 lead that held up as the series-clincher. (CLE)
  • Gavin Williams [5.2 IP, 0 ER, 12 K | 3.76 ERA, PAR 49] was dominant for Cleveland in the winner-take-all Game 5. (CLE)
  • Sean Burke [5 IP, 2 ER, 4 K | 3.35 ERA, PAR 48] pitched well in defeat for the White Sox. (CWS)
  • Cade Smith [1.2 IP, 0 ER, 4 K | 1.95 ERA, PAR 32] and Hunter Gaddis [1.1 IP, 0 ER, 4 K | 3.00 ERA, PAR 17] combined for three scoreless innings of relief to help close out the series. (CLE)
  • Petey Halpin [2-3 | RC 16] chipped in a multi-hit game for the Guardians. (CLE)

The Guardians evened the AL Division Series 2-2 with a 9-5 win at Rate Field, erasing a 4-3 deficit entering the sixth to force a decisive Game 5 with both teams facing elimination. The comeback was keyed by José Ramírez [2-5, 1 HR | RC 56]'s go-ahead homer, the game's decisive swing.

  • José Ramírez flipped the game with a top-5th two-run homer that scored Steven Kwan [1-3, 2 BB | RC 72], putting Cleveland ahead 3-2 en route to the 9-5 win and a 2-2 series tie. (CLE)
  • Patrick Bailey [2-3, 1 HR | RC 28] added a homer and reached base twice as part of Cleveland's rally. (CLE)
  • Nathaniel Lowe [2-4, 1 BB | RC 54] chipped in a multi-hit day in the win. (CLE)
  • Shawn Armstrong [1.2 IP, 0 ER, 2 K | 4.62 ERA, PAR 6] and Hunter Gaddis [1.1 IP, 0 ER, 1 K | 3.00 ERA, PAR 17] combined for three scoreless innings of relief to protect the lead. (CLE)
  • Miguel Vargas [1-2, 3 BB, 1 HR | RC 101] homered for the White Sox in the loss. (CWS)
  • Tyler Davis [2 IP, 0 ER, 1 K | 3.66 ERA, PAR 7] delivered two scoreless innings in relief for Chicago. (CWS)

Three Division Series ended on October 7, with the Rays sweeping the Yankees, the Dodgers closing out the Braves, and the Brewers finishing off the Padres. The lone series still alive is in the AL Central, where the White Sox lead the Guardians 2-1 and Cleveland now faces elimination in Game 4.

  • Victor Mesa Jr. [1-4, 1 HR | RC 38]'s top-6th two-run homer put Tampa Bay ahead for good in a 4-3 win over the Yankees, completing a 3-0 sweep. (TB)
  • Andy Pages [2-3 | RC 82]'s top-7th two-run single broke open a 4-1 Dodgers win in Atlanta, clinching the NLDS 3-1. (LAD)
  • Fernando Tatis Jr. [1-3, 1 BB, 1 HR | RC 105]'s bottom-3rd solo homer briefly tied it, but Milwaukee pulled away for a 3-1 win and a 3-1 series clincher over San Diego. (SD)
  • Jo Adell [2-4, 1 BB | RC 72]'s top-3rd three-run triple fueled Cleveland's 9-3 rout of the White Sox, the day's biggest comeback after the Guardians trailed 1-0; Chicago still leads the series 2-1. (CLE)
  • Tyler Mahle [6.1 IP, 1 ER, 4 K | 3.99 ERA, PAR 33] was sharp in a losing effort for Atlanta. (ATL)
  • Foster Griffin [2.2 IP, 1 ER, 7 K | 3.61 ERA, PAR 42] struck out seven in relief for Cleveland. (CLE)

Both NL Division Series shifted on Tuesday, with the Dodgers taking a 2-1 lead over the Braves and the Padres cutting the Brewers' lead to 2-1. Atlanta and San Diego now face elimination in Game 4.

  • Enrique Hernández [1-4, 1 HR]'s two-run homer in the top of the 4th broke the game open as the Dodgers beat the Braves 3-1 to take a 2-1 series lead. (LAD)
  • Christian Yelich [2-4, 1 BB | RC 53]'s 9th-inning double play ended the Brewers' rally, giving the Padres a 4-3 win and cutting Milwaukee's series lead to 2-1. (MIL)
  • Yoshinobu Yamamoto [7 IP, 1 ER, 10 K | 2.53 ERA, PAR 63] dominated Atlanta over 7 innings, leading all pitchers in PAR on the day. (LAD)
  • William Contreras [3-4, 1 BB, 1 HR | RC 80] had the top batting line of the day in a losing effort for Milwaukee. (MIL)
  • Jake Cronenworth [2-2, 1 HR | RC 37] homered in the Padres' comeback win. (SD)
  • Chris Sale [5 IP, 3 ER, 7 K | 2.16 ERA, PAR 68] turned in a strong start for the Braves but took the loss. (ATL)

Both AL Division Series favorites fell into 2-0 holes, with Cleveland and New York now facing elimination in Game 3. The White Sox pulled off the day's biggest comeback, rallying from a 2-1 deficit in the sixth to beat the Guardians.

  • Braden Montgomery [1-4 | RC 35]'s go-ahead double in the top of the 6th flipped the game and put the White Sox up 3-2 en route to a 4-3 win, giving Chicago a 2-0 series lead and pushing Cleveland to the brink. (CWS)
  • Junior Caminero [2-4 | RC 116]'s double in the bottom of the 5th tied the game and sparked the Rays' 5-2 win over the Yankees, giving Tampa Bay a 2-0 series lead with New York facing elimination. (TB)
  • Sean Burke [5.1 IP, 1 ER, 6 K | 3.35 ERA, PAR 48] led all pitchers on the day in his start for the White Sox. (CWS)
  • Gavin Williams [5 IP, 2 ER, 11 K | 3.76 ERA, PAR 49] struck out 11 in a losing effort for Cleveland. (CLE)
  • Ben Rice [2-3, 1 BB, 2 HR | RC 111] homered twice for the Yankees in the loss. (NYY)
  • Freddy Peralta [4.2 IP, 1 ER, 3 K | 4.42 ERA, PAR 31] turned in a strong start for the Rays. (TB)

The Milwaukee Brewers took a commanding 2-0 lead over the San Diego Padres in their NL Division Series, rallying from a deep deficit to pull off the day's biggest comeback and push the Padres to the brink of elimination. In the other NLDS, the Atlanta Braves evened their series with the Los Angeles Dodgers at 1-1 with a 3-2 road win.

  • Milwaukee defeated San Diego 4-3 at American Family Field, erasing a deep deficit to seize a 2-0 series lead; the Padres face elimination in Game 3. (PADRES)
  • Atlanta beat Los Angeles 3-2 at Dodger Stadium to tie their NLDS at 1-1.
  • Michael King [5 IP, 1 ER, 6 K | 3.21 ERA, PAR 48] turned in the day's best pitching line for San Diego in a losing effort, while Logan Henderson [5 IP, 1 ER, 4 K | 2.48 ERA, PAR 34] was strong for the Brewers. (SD)
  • Didier Fuentes [3.2 IP, 1 ER, 3 K | 2.46 ERA, PAR 28] and reliever Ray Kerr [2.2 IP, 0 ER, 4 K | 1.49 ERA, PAR 7] anchored Atlanta's pitching effort in the win. (ATL)
  • Freddie Freeman [2-4, 1 HR | RC 90] homered and led all batters at the plate, and Max Muncy [1-3, 1 HR | RC 83] also went deep for the Dodgers in the loss. (LAD)
  • Michael Harris II [3-5 | RC 93] paced the Braves' offense with a three-hit game. (ATL)

Day 1 of the Division Series produced a mixed bag, with all four Game 1 winners now holding 1-0 series leads. The Brewers authored the day's most dramatic turn, climbing from a 27% win probability to beat the Padres 3-2 in the day's biggest WPA swing.

  • Brewers 3, Padres 2: Milwaukee rallied from a low of 27% win probability to take Game 1; William Contreras [1-3, 1 BB, 1 HR | RC 80] homered. (MIL)
  • Rays 1, Yankees 0: Drew Rasmussen [8 IP, 0 ER, 10 K | 2.67 ERA, PAR 62] dominated with the day's top pitching line, outdueling Gerrit Cole [5 IP, 1 ER, 5 K | 3.61 ERA, PAR 31] in a tight Game 1. (TB)
  • Dodgers 5, Braves 3: Tarik Skubal [6 IP, 1 ER, 7 K | 2.73 ERA, PAR 59] turned in a strong start, while Teoscar Hernández [2-4, 1 HR | RC 63] and Kyle Tucker [2-4, 1 HR | RC 69] each homered; Ozzie Albies [1-3, 1 BB, 1 HR | RC 71] went deep for Atlanta. (LAD)
  • White Sox 3, Guardians 0: Grant Taylor [4 IP, 0 ER, 6 K | 2.25 ERA, PAR 33] was sharp in relief/short start and Munetaka Murakami [2-4, 1 HR | RC 75] provided the power with a home run. (CWS)
  • All four Division Series stand 1-0 after Game 1; no team faces elimination in Game 2.

The Atlanta Braves clinched the NL Wild Card Series with a 6-2 win over the Philadelphia Phillies in Game 3, eliminating Philadelphia and advancing to the NLDS. Atlanta rallied from behind in the decisive game, which also produced the day's largest WPA swing.

  • Braves 6, Phillies 2: Atlanta took the best-of-3 series 2-1, erasing an earlier deficit to clinch. (PHILLIES)
  • Matt Olson [1-3, 1 BB, 1 HR | RC 101], Michael Harris II [1-3, 1 BB, 1 HR | RC 93], and Ozzie Albies [1-3, 1 BB, 1 HR | RC 71] each homered to power the Atlanta offense. (ATL)
  • Ray Kerr [3.1 IP, 0 ER, 2 K | 1.49 ERA, PAR 7] delivered the day's top pitching line out of the Atlanta bullpen, with Chris Sale [1.1 IP, 0 ER, 3 K | 2.16 ERA, PAR 68] adding scoreless relief work. (ATL)
  • Zack Wheeler [4 IP, 2 ER, 3 K | 3.00 ERA, PAR 51] was Philadelphia's best arm in the loss, and Kyle Schwarber [2-3, 1 BB | RC 103] led the Phillies at the plate. (PHI)

The Phillies pulled off the day's most dramatic result, rallying from an 11% win probability to beat the first-place Braves 4-3 at Truist Park in the game with the biggest WPA swing of the day. The loss doesn't shake Atlanta's grip on the NL East, but Philadelphia closed to within 6.0 games with the comeback win.

  • Alec Bohm [2-4, 1 BB, 1 HR | RC 68] homered as the Phillies stunned the Braves 4-3 in the day's most dramatic game, overcoming an 11% win probability. (PHI)
  • Tyler Mahle [7 IP, 1 ER, 6 K | 3.99 ERA, PAR 33] was the day's top pitcher despite the Braves' loss, delivering 7 strong innings. (ATL)
  • The White Sox beat the Astros 7-3 behind a home run from Chase Meidroth [2-3, 1 BB, 1 HR | RC 82], pulling Chicago to 84-78 and keeping them 1.0 game back in the AL Central. (CWS)
  • The Yankees cruised past the Red Sox 9-2 as Max Fried [6 IP, 1 ER, 6 K | 2.81 ERA, PAR 41] dominated and Luis García Jr. [3-5, 1 HR | RC 83] homered in a 3-for-5 night. (NYY)
  • Willson Contreras [2-2, 2 BB, 1 HR | RC 89] posted the day's top batting line with a 2-for-2, 1 HR effort in Boston's loss. (BOS)
  • The Padres beat the Cubs 4-1, with Gavin Sheets [1-1, 1 HR | RC 45] homering as part of a strong team effort. (SD)
  • Cristopher Sánchez [6.2 IP, 3 ER, 6 K | 2.91 ERA, PAR 72] added a strong 6.2-inning start in Philadelphia's comeback win, and Andrew Painter [3 IP, 0 ER, 3 K | 5.42 ERA, PAR 13] turned in 3 scoreless innings of relief to earn the win. (PHI)

The Braves erased an 80% win-probability deficit to beat the Phillies in the day's most dramatic game, pushing Philadelphia 6.0 back in the NL East with the regular season winding down. Elsewhere, the Yankees and Padres delivered shutout routs behind dominant starts.

  • Chris Sale [6.1 IP, 3 ER, 9 K | 2.16 ERA, PAR 68] and the Braves rallied past the Phillies 5-3 in the day's biggest comeback, with Michael Harris [1-2 | RC 18] II [3-3 | RC 93] leading the offense. (ATL)
  • Cam Schlittler [6.1 IP, 0 ER, 10 K | 1.96 ERA, PAR 80] dominated as the Yankees blanked the Red Sox 9-0, powered by a huge day from Ben Rice [4-5, 2 HR | RC 111]. (NYY)
  • Michael King [7 IP, 0 ER, 8 K | 3.21 ERA, PAR 48] tossed seven shutout innings as the Padres crushed the Cubs 8-0, with Fernando Tatis Jr. [2-3, 1 BB, 1 HR | RC 105], Manny Machado [2-3, 1 BB, 1 HR | RC 73], and Xander Bogaerts [2-4, 1 HR | RC 59] all going deep. (SD)
  • The White Sox beat the Astros 6-3 to pull within 1.0 game of the Guardians in the AL Central. (SOX) (ASTROS)
  • Jesús Luzardo [5 IP, 1 ER, 6 K | 2.86 ERA, PAR 63] turned in a strong start in the Phillies' loss. (PHI)

The Nationals authored the day's most memorable moment, storming back from a 21% win probability to knock off the Mets 6-4 in the day's biggest comeback. Meanwhile, the Dodgers' 5-1 win over the Giants featured the largest WPA swing of the day, as Los Angeles maintains its NL West lead.

  • Andrés Chaparro [3-4, 2 HR | RC 38] powered Washington's comeback win over New York, which fell to 21% win probability before rallying. (WSH)
  • The Dodgers beat the Giants 5-1 in the day's most dramatic game by WPA swing. (DODGERS)
  • Alex Bregman [4-4, 1 BB, 2 HR | RC 100] led the Cubs past the Red Sox 6-2 with a monster day at the plate. (CHC)
  • Max Scherzer [7 IP, 1 ER, 7 K | 5.77 ERA, PAR 5] dominated as the Blue Jays beat the Reds 5-1. (TOR)
  • Christian Walker [2-3, 2 BB, 1 HR | RC 73] and the Astros blanked the Athletics 9-0. (HOU)
  • Zack Wheeler [6 IP, 1 ER, 5 K | 3.00 ERA, PAR 51] carried the Phillies to a 7-3 win over the Rays. (PHI)
  • The Royals edged the Guardians 3-2 behind Vinnie Pasquantino [2-4, 2 HR | RC 60]'s two-homer game, in a contest with the day's second-largest WPA swing. (KC)
  • Baltimore at New York (Yankees) was cancelled.
